name: AD7606BSTZ
title: 8-, 6- and 4-channel simultaneous-sampling 16-bit ADC with bipolar inputs
summary: The AD7606, AD7606-6 and AD7606-4 convert eight, six or four true bipolar inputs (±10 V or ±5 V) at up to 200 kSPS per channel from a single 5 V supply. Each channel has its own clamp, 1 MΩ input, second-order antialiasing filter and track-and-hold, all sampled at once and converted by one 16-bit SAR. An internal 2.5 V reference, a pin-selected oversampling filter and parallel, byte or serial outputs on a 2.3 V to 5.25 V logic supply complete it.
key_figures: 95.5 dB typ (OS × 16, ±10 V); 90 dB typ without OS
AVCC 4.75 V to 5.25 V; VDRIVE 2.3 V to 5.25 V
100 mW typ at 200 kSPS (AD7606); 25 mW standby

notes: The EVAL boards work on their own or together with the CED1Z, which lets a PC control and talk to Analog Devices evaluation boards whose names end in EDZ.

pins.name: AVCC
pins.function: Analog supply, 4.75 V to 5.25 V, feeding the front-end amplifiers and the converter core. Decouple to AGND.

pins.name: AGND
pins.function: Analog ground: the reference point for all analog circuitry, analog inputs and external reference. Connect every AGND pin to the system's AGND plane.

pins.name: OS 0
pins.function: Oversampling ratio select, least significant bit of OS[2:0].

pins.name: OS 1
pins.function: Oversampling ratio select, middle bit of OS[2:0].

pins.name: OS 2
pins.function: Oversampling ratio select, most significant bit of OS[2:0].

pins.name: PAR/SER/BYTE SEL
pins.function: Interface select. Low: parallel. High: serial, or parallel byte when DB15/BYTE SEL is also high. In serial mode RD/SCLK becomes the clock, DB7 and DB8 become DOUTA and DOUTB, and DB[15:9] and DB[6:0] go to ground.

pins.name: STBY
pins.function: Power-down control, active low. The level on RANGE picks standby (reference and regulators stay on) or shutdown (everything off).

pins.name: RANGE
pins.function: Input range for every channel: high gives ±10 V, low gives ±5 V. Takes effect at once; changing it during a conversion is not advised at fast throughput. Also picks the power-down mode while STBY is low.

pins.name: CONVST A
pins.function: Conversion start for the first channel set (V1 to V4 on the AD7606, V1 to V3 on the AD7606-6, V1 and V2 on the AD7606-4). A rising edge puts those track-and-holds into hold. Tie to CONVST B to sample every channel together.

pins.name: CONVST B
pins.function: Conversion start for the second channel set (V5 to V8 on the AD7606, V4 to V6 on the AD7606-6, V3 and V4 on the AD7606-4). Separate CONVST A and B timing works only with oversampling off.

pins.name: RESET
pins.function: Reset. A rising edge resets the part; pulse it after power-up (typically 50 ns high). A reset during a conversion aborts it; during a read it clears the output registers to zero.

pins.name: RD/SCLK
pins.function: Parallel mode: read strobe; with CS low the output bus is driven. Serial mode: serial clock; after the CS falling edge has put out the MSB, each rising edge shifts the next bit onto DOUTA and DOUTB.

pins.name: CS
pins.function: Chip select, active low. Frames a transfer: with RD low it drives DB[15:0] in parallel mode; in serial mode it frames the read and puts out the MSB.

pins.name: BUSY
pins.function: Rises after the later of the CONVST A and CONVST B rising edges and stays high until every channel is converted. Its falling edge latches the results into the output registers, readable after t4. A read under BUSY high must end before that edge; CONVST edges are ignored while BUSY is high.

pins.name: FRSTDATA
pins.function: Marks the V1 result. Three-state while CS is high. Parallel and byte modes: high from the RD falling edge that outputs V1 until the next RD falling edge. Serial mode: high from the CS falling edge until the 16th SCLK falling edge.

pins.name: DB0
pins.function: Parallel data bit 0, three-state while CS or RD is high. Tie to AGND when PAR/SER/BYTE SEL = 1. In byte mode DB[7:0] carry each result as two bytes, DB0 the LSB.

pins.name: DB1
pins.function: Parallel data bit 1, three-state while CS or RD is high. Tie to AGND when PAR/SER/BYTE SEL = 1. In byte mode DB[7:0] carry each result as two bytes, DB0 the LSB.

pins.name: DB2
pins.function: Parallel data bit 2, three-state while CS or RD is high. Tie to AGND when PAR/SER/BYTE SEL = 1. In byte mode DB[7:0] carry each result as two bytes, DB0 the LSB.

pins.name: DB3
pins.function: Parallel data bit 3, three-state while CS or RD is high. Tie to AGND when PAR/SER/BYTE SEL = 1. In byte mode DB[7:0] carry each result as two bytes, DB0 the LSB.

pins.name: DB4
pins.function: Parallel data bit 4, three-state while CS or RD is high. Tie to AGND when PAR/SER/BYTE SEL = 1. In byte mode DB[7:0] carry each result as two bytes, DB0 the LSB.

pins.name: DB5
pins.function: Parallel data bit 5, three-state while CS or RD is high. Tie to AGND when PAR/SER/BYTE SEL = 1. In byte mode DB[7:0] carry each result as two bytes, DB0 the LSB.

pins.name: DB6
pins.function: Parallel data bit 6, three-state while CS or RD is high. Tie to AGND when PAR/SER/BYTE SEL = 1. In byte mode DB[7:0] carry each result as two bytes, DB0 the LSB.

pins.name: VDRIVE

circuits.title: Typical connection
circuits.description: An AD7606 on its internal reference, read over the parallel bus by a processor. REF SELECT, RANGE and STBY are pulled to VDRIVE (internal reference, ±10 V range, normal operation) and PAR/SER SEL to ground (parallel interface). The host drives the joined CONVST A and CONVST B, CS, RD, RESET and the three OS lines, reads DB0 to DB15 and watches BUSY. A 10 µF capacitor decouples REFIN/REFOUT, a second 10 µF the joined REFCAPA and REFCAPB pins against REFGND, 1 µF each REGCAP pin, and 100 nF each AVCC pin and VDRIVE. All eight VxGND pins go to analog ground; VDRIVE comes from the processor's own supply.

parts.note: one on each REGCAP pin (36 and 39)
one on each AVCC pin (1, 37, 38, 48); pins 37 and 38 may share one

notes: A 10 µF capacitor also sits at the source of the analog supply.

circuits.title: One external reference for several devices
circuits.description: An ADR421 supplies 2.5 V to the REFIN/REFOUT pins of three AD7606 devices. Each device has REF SELECT pulled low, so its internal reference is off and the pin is a high-impedance input, and each REFIN/REFOUT pin has its own 100 nF capacitor; the ADR421 output has 0.1 µF.

circuits.title: One device's internal reference for several devices
circuits.description: The first AD7606 has REF SELECT pulled to VDRIVE, so its internal 2.5 V reference is on and comes out on REFIN/REFOUT, decoupled by 10 µF. That pin feeds REFIN/REFOUT of two more AD7606 devices whose REF SELECT is pulled low (external reference mode); each of them has 100 nF on the pin.

circuits.title: One device on the parallel bus with CS and RD joined
circuits.description: A single AD7606 that has the parallel bus to itself is read with one control line: CS (pin 13) and RD (pin 12) are joined and driven by the host, BUSY (pin 14) goes to a host interrupt, and DB[15:0] (pins 16 to 22, 24, 25 and 27 to 33) form the data bus. Each falling edge of the joined line brings the next channel's result onto the bus.

circuits.title: Matched series resistance on an analog input
circuits.description: A series resistor R carries the signal into Vx and an equal resistor R joins VxGND to ground, with a capacitor C between Vx and VxGND. Matching the resistance on VxGND to the one on Vx avoids an offset error on that channel; the resistor on Vx also limits clamp current to ±10 mA when the input exceeds ±16.5 V. The same arrangement applies to each input Vx and its VxGND.

operation.text: Each input has a clamp, a 1 MΩ input resistor feeding a scaling amplifier, a second-order Butterworth antialiasing filter and its own track-and-hold. One 16-bit charge-redistribution SAR converts the held channels in turn through an 8:1 multiplexer, followed by an optional digital filter. An on-chip 2.5 V reference is buffered up to about 4.5 V for the SAR. Results leave by parallel, byte-wide or serial interface. The part runs from one 5 V analog supply plus a 2.3 V to 5.25 V logic supply.

AD7606: eight channels. AD7606-6: six. AD7606-4: four. All three share the 64-lead LQFP pinout; positions a smaller variant does not use become AGND pins, and the remaining inputs are renumbered in order.

RANGE high gives ±10 V on every channel, low gives ±5 V. A change acts at once but needs roughly 80 µs to settle on top of the normal acquisition time, so RANGE is best wired to a fixed level. Pulsing RESET once powered sets the channels to the selected range. Inputs should stay inside the chosen range in normal use.
The input impedance is a fixed 1 MΩ whatever the sample rate, so a source or sensor can connect directly without a driver amplifier or bipolar supplies.

No clamp current flows for inputs within ±16.5 V; beyond that the clamp conducts. A series resistor should hold the current to ±10 mA for inputs past ±16.5 V, and any series resistance on Vx needs an equal resistance on VxGND or that channel gains an offset error. The clamp is meant for transient overvoltage only: leaving it conducting for long periods, in normal operation or power-down, can degrade bipolar zero code error and THD. In power-down the inputs should be tied to GND.
Second-order Butterworth. The −3 dB point is typically 15 kHz on the ±5 V range and 23 kHz on ±10 V; at 200 kSPS the filter rejects aliases by 40 dB.

All track-and-holds go into hold on the CONVST x rising edge. Their aperture delay is matched by design across the channels of one part and between parts, so several devices can sample at the same instant. On the BUSY falling edge they return to track and the next acquisition starts.

The conversion clock is internal. Converting all channels takes 4 µs (AD7606), 3 µs (AD7606-6) or 2 µs (AD7606-4). BUSY rises when conversion starts and falls when the last channel is done; new data can be read after that, or the previous result read during BUSY high. Reading in parallel mode during a conversion at VDRIVE above 3.3 V costs about 1.5 dB of SNR.

Output coding is twos complement with code transitions at 1/2 LSB and 3/2 LSB steps. LSB = FSR/65,536. Ideal last transition: 10 V − 1½ LSB (9.99954 V) or 5 V − 1½ LSB (4.99977 V); ideal first transition: −10 V + ½ LSB (−9.99984 V) or −5 V + ½ LSB (−4.99992 V); midscale transition at 0 V − ½ LSB.

REF SELECT high enables the internal 2.5 V bandgap and puts it on REFIN/REFOUT; low turns it off and REFIN/REFOUT becomes a high-impedance input for an external 2.5 V. Either way an internal buffer, always on, gains the reference to about 4.5 V for the SAR. After a reset the part uses whichever mode REF SELECT selects. REFIN/REFOUT needs a 10 µF ceramic capacitor; REFCAPA and REFCAPB must be shorted together outside the part with a 10 µF ceramic to REFGND so the buffer runs closed loop.

Either one ADR421 feeds every device's REFIN/REFOUT, each pin with at least 100 nF, or one device in internal mode drives the rest in external mode: its REFIN/REFOUT gets 10 µF ceramic and each of the others at least 100 nF.

Each of the four AVCC pins takes 100 nF at the pin, with 10 µF at the supply source; pins 37 and 38 may share one 100 nF. Each REGCAP pin takes its own 1 µF. VDRIVE should come from the same supply as the processor and sets the output logic levels. After the supplies come up a reset puts the part in the right mode.

A RESET pulse is required after power-up, typically 50 ns wide. Reset during a conversion aborts it; reset during a read clears the output registers to all zeros. After waking from shutdown a reset must follow once the power-up time has passed.

STBY low selects power-down; RANGE then picks the mode. Standby (RANGE = 1): reference and regulators stay on, amplifiers and converter core are off, current at most 8 mA, about 100 µs to wake while the REFCAPA/REFCAPB capacitor recharges. Shutdown (RANGE = 0): all circuitry off, current at most 6 µA, about 13 ms to wake with an external reference (30 ms with the internal one).

With CONVST A and CONVST B tied together, one rising edge samples every channel at once. BUSY goes high on that edge and low at the end of conversion, returning all track-and-holds to track and signalling that new data are on DB[15:0], DOUTA/DOUTB or DB[7:0].

With oversampling off, CONVST A and CONVST B may be pulsed separately: A holds the first set (V1 to V4, V1 to V3, or V1 and V2) and B the second (V5 to V8, V4 to V6, or V3 and V4). Conversion starts after both edges, so BUSY rises on the later one; t5 limits their spacing. In power-line systems this offsets PT and CT phase errors by up to 9° at 50 Hz and 10° at 60 Hz. Reading is the same as with one CONVST.
Unused analog inputs go to AGND. Every channel is always converted, so unused channels still appear in the read-out.

PAR/SER/BYTE SEL low. CS and RD are gated inside the part: DB15 to DB0 leave high impedance only when both are low. Each RD falling edge moves to the next result, V1 first; on the AD7606 the eighth gives V8. CS may be held low with RD strobing, which lets several devices share the bus through their CS lines; a lone device that owns the bus can run with CS and RD joined, the bus coming out of three-state on their common falling edge. A read of new data follows BUSY falling, or the previous result read during BUSY high.

Both interface-select pins (PAR/SER/BYTE SEL, DB15/BYTE SEL) high. Results come out on DB[7:0], DB7 the MSB and DB0 the LSB, two reads per channel: 16 RD pulses for the AD7606, 12 for the AD7606-6, 8 for the AD7606-4. DB14/HBEN high sends the high byte first, low the low byte first. FRSTDATA stays high until both bytes of V1 have been read.

PAR/SER/BYTE SEL high, DB15/BYTE SEL low. The CS falling edge takes DOUTA and DOUTB out of three-state and puts out the MSB, valid on the first SCLK falling edge; each SCLK rising edge shifts out one of the remaining 15 bits, valid on the falling edge, so each result takes 16 clocks. DOUTA carries V1 to V4 (V1 to V3, V1 and V2 on the smaller variants) and DOUTB the rest, so two lines read an AD7606 in 64 clocks. One line needs 128 clocks for the AD7606 and lowers throughput when reading after conversion; DOUTA is the preferred single line because it gives the channels in ascending order. Read on DOUTB alone the order is V5 to V8 then V1 to V4 (AD7606), V4 to V6 then V1 to V3 (AD7606-6), V3, V4, V1, V2 (AD7606-4). CS may stay low for the whole read or frame each 16-clock word. The unused DOUT line is left open.

FRSTDATA flags the V1 result and is three-state while CS is high. In serial mode it goes high on the CS falling edge and low after the 16th SCLK falling edge. It only tracks DOUTA: reading DOUTB alone it does not go high for V1 (it is high while V5 comes out on DOUTB, on the AD7606).

Data may be read during BUSY high, with or without oversampling, in any interface mode, with little effect on performance and a higher throughput; it is what lets the serial interface reach full throughput with VDRIVE above 4.75 V. The only forbidden moment is the BUSY falling edge, when the output registers update; t6 applies.

OS[2:0] select an optional first-order sinc filter, OS 2 the MSB; code 111 is invalid. OS levels are captured at each BUSY falling edge and apply to the next conversion. At ratio N the CONVST edge takes the first sample of every channel and an internal clock takes the other N − 1; the samples are averaged and the result decimated to 16 bits. SNR rises with N while the 3 dB bandwidth and the highest sampling rate fall, and BUSY stays high longer. Both CONVST pins must be joined with oversampling on. For example, a 10 kSPS application can use OS up to 16, giving better SNR with a bandwidth near 6 kHz. Reading during BUSY gives the fastest throughput with oversampling on.
For a DC input the spread of output codes narrows as the oversampling ratio rises: six codes with no oversampling down to two from OS × 16 upward.
The analog antialiasing filter followed by the oversampling filter can remove or simplify filtering in front of the part; the digital filter rolls off steeply with linear phase.

Keep analog and digital sections in separate areas. Use at least one ground plane, common or split; split analog and digital planes join at one point as close to the part as possible, and in a system of several such parts the join is a single star point near them. Give each ground pin its own via or vias rather than sharing. Run no digital lines under the part, and let the analog ground plane run beneath it. Shield fast signals such as CONVST A, CONVST B and clocks with digital ground and keep them away from analog paths; avoid digital and analog crossovers, and run traces on adjacent layers at right angles. Feed AVCC and VDRIVE with wide traces or planes, one or more vias per supply pin.

Put decoupling capacitors right against their supply pins and the matching ground pins. The REFIN/REFOUT, REFCAPA and REFCAPB capacitors go as near their pins as they will go, preferably on the part's own board side. With the AVCC 100 nF capacitors at their pins, pins 37 and 38 may share one.

Lay several devices out symmetrically for good matching. In the two-device example the AVCC plane runs on one side of both parts and the VDRIVE track on the other, the reference sits between them with its track running north to pin 42 of one and south to pin 42 of the other, over a solid ground plane. More devices extend the same north-south arrangement with the reference in the middle.

Bipolar zero code error: how far the midscale step (all 1s to all 0s) sits from its ideal point, 0 V − ½ LSB. Positive and negative full-scale error: how far the last and first code steps sit from ideal once bipolar zero code error is taken out, including the internal reference buffer. A matching figure is the absolute difference of that error between any two channels. Channel-to-channel isolation: attenuation seen in a channel carrying a 1 kHz sine when a full-scale sine up to 160 kHz drives all the other channels. Peak harmonic or spurious noise: largest spectral component other than the fundamental, up to fS/2 excluding DC, relative to the fundamental. Intermodulation products with inputs fa and fb fall at mfa ± nfb with neither m nor n zero; second order (fa + fb), (fa − fb), third order (2fa ± fb), (fa ± 2fb).
